dmTitle.infoName: Data Recording, Storage, and Retrieval Logic

levelledPara.title: Introduction
levelledPara.para: This data module describes the data recording, storage, and retrieval mechanisms for the AMPEL360 Q100 Indicating and Recording System. The system implements multiple recording strategies to support regulatory compliance (FDR/CVR), operational quality (QAR/FOQA), predictive maintenance (ACMS), and digital product lifecycle management (DPP integration).

levelledPara.title: Recording Parameters
levelledPara.para: FDR records minimum 88 parameters per ED-112A requirements, including:

- Flight control positions (elevator, aileron, rudder, trim)
- Engine/propulsion parameters (fuel cell voltage/current, motor speed/torque)
- Air data (airspeed, altitude, angle-of-attack, vertical speed)
- Navigation (position, heading, track)
- System status (gear position, flap position, warnings/alerts)
- Time stamps (UTC synchronized)

levelledPara.title: Recording Logic
levelledPara.para: FDR recording initiated when:

- Aircraft electrical power applied (any power source)
- Recording continues until power removed
- Minimum 25-hour capacity with circular buffer (oldest data overwritten)
- Recording rate: 1 Hz (slow parameters) to 64 Hz (flight controls)
- Data encoding: ARINC 647 or binary as appropriate
- Crash survivability: Memory module survives 3,400g impact, 1,100°C for 1 hour, 20,000 ft seawater immersion

levelledPara.title: Data Integrity
levelledPara.para: FDR implements multiple data integrity mechanisms:

- Cyclic redundancy check (CRC) on each data frame
- Cryptographic hash chain for tamper detection
- Error correction coding on memory storage
- Dual redundant memory banks with cross-checking
- Write verification after each commit
- Independent clock/timing verification

levelledPara.title: Data Retrieval
levelledPara.para: FDR data retrieved by:

- Direct readout via maintenance port (requires specialized equipment)
- Memory module removal for laboratory analysis (accident investigation)
- Wireless download via secure datalink (if equipped, requires authorization)
- Data format: Standardized per ED-112A for readability by NTSB/BEA analysis tools

levelledPara.title: Audio Sources
levelledPara.para: CVR records four independent audio channels:

- Channel 1: Captain microphone
- Channel 2: First Officer microphone
- Channel 3: Cockpit area microphone (ambient sounds)
- Channel 4: Spare / Third crew position (if applicable)

levelledPara.title: Recording Logic
levelledPara.para: CVR recording initiated when:

- Aircraft electrical power applied OR
- Engines/motors running (via discrete input)
- Minimum 2-hour capacity with circular buffer
- Audio encoding: Digital compression (typically ADPCM or similar)
- Recording quality: Sufficient intelligibility for accident investigation

levelledPara.title: Erase Function
levelledPara.para: CVR includes crew-initiated erase function (regulatory requirement):

- Erase switch located in cockpit (typically overhead panel)
- Erase enabled only when aircraft on ground AND parking brake set
- Erase requires sustained switch actuation (5 seconds) to prevent inadvertent activation
- Erase operation overwrites all audio with zeros/silence
- Erase event logged in FDR and ACMS
- WARNING: Erase function disabled during accident/incident investigation per regulatory lock-out

levelledPara.title: Purpose and Scope
levelledPara.para: QAR provides easily accessible flight data for operational quality monitoring:

- Superset of FDR parameters (typically 200-500 parameters)
- Higher recording rates (up to 8 Hz) for engineering analysis
- Removable memory module for ground data transfer
- Storage capacity: 100-500 flight hours (depends on parameter count)
- Data used for FOQA, pilot training, fuel efficiency analysis

levelledPara.title: Data Download Process
levelledPara.para: QAR data downloaded by:

1. Remove QAR memory module from aircraft
2. Insert module into ground station reader
3. Transfer data to FOQA analysis system
4. Return module to aircraft or install fresh module
5. Data typically downloaded weekly or after each flight (airline operational practice)

levelledPara.title: ACMS Data Collection
levelledPara.para: ACMS aggregates maintenance-relevant data from all aircraft systems:

- Fault codes and BITE results from all LRUs
- System usage statistics (cycles, hours, actuations)
- Trending data (temperatures, pressures, vibration levels)
- Configuration changes and software updates
- Maintenance actions and part replacements

levelledPara.title: Automatic Reporting
levelledPara.para: ACMS automatically generates and transmits reports:

- Post-flight report: Generated at engine/motor shutdown, transmitted via datalink
- Event-triggered reports: Sent immediately when critical fault detected
- Scheduled reports: Daily or weekly summaries of fleet health
- Integration with airline maintenance systems and OEM support
- Reports formatted per ARINC 624 or proprietary airline standards

levelledPara.title: Lifecycle Data Recording
levelledPara.para: Recording system contributes data to aircraft Digital Product Passport (ATA 95):

- Component installation dates and serial numbers
- Cumulative usage (flight hours, cycles, landings)
- Maintenance events and corrective actions
- Environmental exposure (temperature extremes, lightning strikes)
- Software and configuration baseline history
- Data archived for aircraft lifetime (30+ years)

levelledPara.title: Data Archival Strategy
levelledPara.para: Long-term data storage architecture:

- On-aircraft: Rolling 90-day cache in non-volatile memory
- Ground systems: Complete flight-by-flight archive in airline/OEM databases
- Cloud storage: Encrypted, redundant, geographically distributed
- Blockchain anchoring: Cryptographic proofs of data existence and integrity
- Access control: Role-based permissions for data retrieval and analysis

levelledPara.title: Cybersecurity and Data Protection
levelledPara.para: All recording systems implement cybersecurity controls:

- Data encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3)
- Authentication of data sources (digital signatures)
- Tamper-evident seals and intrusion detection
- Audit logging of all data access and modifications
- Compliance with DO-326A cybersecurity requirements
- Regular security assessments and penetration testing
